name: The Teen Idles
label: Dischord
lede: Four kids from Wilson High, one Greyhound trip to California, six hundred dollars in savings, and a thousand hand-glued sleeves that became Dischord No. 1.

eras.title: The Cramps did it
eras.text: D.C. punk in early 1979 was a handful of shows and a handful of kids. A few of them went to Woodrow Wilson High School, saw The Cramps at the Hall of Nations, and started a band before they could legally get into most of the clubs.

q: The first show that made us want to be in a band
years.h: Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson see the Cramps at the Hall of Nations
years.p: [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] see [[The Cramps|96c1edac-1011-4cb8-882c-27248de35071]] at Georgetown's Hall of Nations. It's the night they decide to be in a band.
years.xp: Ian MacKaye later said that until the Cramps show, Ted Nugent was about as wild as music got for him. The Cramps ended that.

years.h: The Slinkees form at Wilson High
years.p: The Slinkees, the band that becomes the Teen Idles: Ian MacKaye on bass, Jeff Nelson on drums, [[Geordie Grindle|2f8ebbdb-3b57-4648-a339-bedf27b86ab3]] on guitar and Mark Sullivan singing, all out of Wilson High.

years.h: Slinkees singer Mark Sullivan leaves for college
years.p: Mark Sullivan goes off to school. Ian MacKaye's friend Henry Garfield, later [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]], can't take the spot, so [[Nathan Strejcek|b53e7b75-696d-43f5-98ff-bc3d104e0d74]] becomes the singer.

years.h: The Slinkees become the Teen Idles
years.p: With Nathan Strejcek singing, the Slinkees rename themselves the Teen Idles. MacKaye, Nelson, Grindle and Strejcek are the lineup that makes Dischord No. 1.

eras.title: Too young to rock, too loud to stop
eras.text: The Teen Idles lasted about a year and a half, and 1980 was nearly all of it. They chased the Bad Brains, got thrown out of clubs for being underage, took a Greyhound to California, and came back with the idea that would outlast them: an X on the back of the hand.

years.h: The Teen Idles get kicked out of clubs for being underage
years.p: Many of the Teen Idles and their friends are under 18, and they want to see the [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]], maybe the greatest band in the world in 1980, as Dischord puts it. Clubs keep showing them the door.

years.h: Pizza parlors, house parties, and opening for Bad Brains
years.p: The Teen Idles' early gigs are house parties and pizza parlors. Wikipedia says they landed a slot opening for [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] at Madam's Organ, an art gallery.

years.h: Greyhound to California, and the X comes home
years.p: The Teen Idles ride the bus west with roadies Mark Sullivan and Henry Garfield, the "fifth Idle." At San Francisco's Mabuhay Gardens, the underage kids get a marker X on their hands so the bar knows not to serve them.
years.xp:
It wasn't a smooth trip. According to Wikipedia, Jeff Nelson spent an hour in police handcuffs soon after they arrived, and in Los Angeles the band was turned away from the Hong Kong Café for being underage.

Back in D.C., they pitched the Mabuhay system to local clubs: mark the kids, let them in. The 9:30 Club adopted it. A few months later an X-marked pair of hands, belonging to Ian MacKaye's younger brother [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]], was on the cover of Minor Disturbance, and the X came to stand for straight edge.

years.h: Guitarist Geordie Grindle quits the Teen Idles
years.p: Per Wikipedia, Geordie Grindle's born-again Christian girlfriend disapproved of the band, and friction with atheist Jeff Nelson built until he quit. That ended the Teen Idles.

years.h: The Teen Idles' last show: opening for SVT at the 9:30 Club
years.p: The Teen Idles play their final set at the 9:30 Club, opening for SVT. Their song Too Young to Rock is taped live that night and goes straight onto Minor Disturbance.

q: Let's give it 100 percent, for a minute and a half
years.p: Recorded in August 1980 with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] and [[Skip Groff|8c4d8d50-a6a7-4fa6-9524-6e9c595816c1]]. The Teen Idles' $600 in savings paid for 1,000 copies, sleeves glued by hand, on a label they invented: Dischord.
years.xp:
The eight songs, about nine minutes, were cut at Inner Ear, then a four-track in Zientara's Arlington home. Zientara described the band as them against the world, playing every song as if they'd collapse at the end of it.

Jeff Nelson designed the cover around Susie Josephson's photo of Alec MacKaye's crossed, X-marked hands. The back cover is Jay Rabinowitz's Halloween 1980 photo of the band and friends outside the Chancery.

years.h: Ian MacKaye takes the mic in [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]
years.p: Ian MacKaye moves from bass to vocals and Jeff Nelson stays on drums in their new band, Minor Threat, which plays its first show before 1980 is out.

eras.title: What six hundred dollars built
eras.text: The Teen Idles were gone, but Minor Disturbance, Dischord No. 1, kept doing its job. Dischord released its friends' bands one 7-inch at a time, roadie Henry Garfield went national as Henry Rollins, and the EP stayed in print alongside the records it made possible.

years.h: Teen Idles roadie Henry Garfield joins [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]]
years.p: Henry Garfield, the "fifth Idle" on the 1980 California trip, leaves D.C. to front Black Flag as Henry Rollins.

years.h: Nathan Strejcek runs Dischord, then loses it
years.p: Former Teen Idles singer Nathan Strejcek takes on running Dischord, but Jeff Nelson and Ian MacKaye, unhappy with how little he put in, take it back. He goes on to front [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]].

years.h: The Teen Idles on Flex Your Head
years.p: Teen Idles tracks land on Dischord No. 7, Flex Your Head, the compilation that mapped early D.C. hardcore.

With the original pressing long gone, Minor Disturbance is gathered onto one LP with the early singles by [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]], [[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]] and Youth Brigade.

eras.title: Dischord No. 100 looks back at No. 1
eras.text: Fifteen years on, Dischord had outlived nearly every band it started with. When the catalog hit No. 100, the label went back to the Teen Idles, the band that made No. 1.

years.p: The Teen Idles' 1980 EP gets its first compact disc release.

years.h: Anniversary: the 1980 demos the studio laughed at
years.p: In 1980 the Teen Idles taped two demo sessions while the engineer and a visiting band laughed at them. Dischord released them as its 100th record in 1996.
years.xp: The demos come from February and April 1980. Dischord chose the band that made No. 1 for No. 100.
